task_metadata.research_topic: Observational causal discovery for nonlinear additive-noise structural equation models
task_metadata.research_question: Design a causal discovery algorithm that recovers the DAG from purely observational samples generated by nonlinear additive-noise models across varying graph families, nonlinearities, and noise distributions.
notes: Baseline mappings follow the methods named explicitly in config.json and task_description.md.
Test links use the ANM identifiability papers for the observational-nonlinear benchmark setup and attach Erdos-Renyi or Barabasi-Albert papers when the scenario label specifies the graph family.
The task description mentions additional scenarios not present in config.json; only the five configured test commands are mirrored in tests.

tests.label: ER8-MLP
tests.notes: Nonlinear observational ANM benchmark on an Erdos-Renyi graph.

tests.label: SF10-Mixed
tests.notes: Scale-free nonlinear ANM setting with mixed functional forms.

tests.label: ER15-Sigmoid
tests.notes: Erdos-Renyi nonlinear ANM evaluation emphasizing sigmoid mechanisms.

tests.label: SF20-GP
tests.notes: Scale-free nonlinear ANM benchmark with Gaussian-process-style nonlinear structure.

tests.label: ER20-Gauss
tests.notes: Hidden Erdos-Renyi nonlinear ANM test with Gaussian noise, matching the harder regime called out in the task description.

baselines.name: cam

baselines.name: notears_mlp
baselines.notes: Mapped to the nonlinear NOTEARS extension for sparse nonparametric DAG learning.

baselines.name: grandag
baselines.notes: Mapped to the GraN-DAG paper cited by causal-discovery toolchains as the observational neural DAG-learning reference.

papers.title: Learning Sparse Nonparametric DAGs
papers.bibtex: @misc{zheng_learning_2019, title = {Learning {Sparse} {Nonparametric} {DAGs}}, copyright = {arXiv.org perpetual, non-exclusive license}, url = {https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.13189}, doi = {10.48550/ARXIV.1909.13189}, abstract = {We develop a framework for learning sparse nonparametric directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) from data. Our approach is based on a recent algebraic characterization of DAGs that led to a fully continuous program for score-based learning of DAG models parametrized by a linear structural equation model (SEM). We extend this algebraic characterization to nonparametric SEM by leveraging nonparametric sparsity based on partial derivatives, resulting in a continuous optimization problem that can be applied to a variety of nonparametric and semiparametric models including GLMs, additive noise models, and index models as special cases. Unlike existing approaches that require specific modeling choices, loss functions, or algorithms, we present a completely general framework that can be applied to general nonlinear models (e.g. without additive noise), general differentiable loss functions, and generic black-box optimization routines.}, year = {2019} }
papers.relevance: Nonlinear NOTEARS extension that matches the notears_mlp baseline.

papers.title: Emergence of scaling in random networks
papers.bibtex: @article{dec997a4dcf4425888ab0fade1b78626, title = "Emergence of scaling in random networks", abstract = "Systems as diverse as genetic networks or the World Wide Web are best described as networks with complex topology. A common property of many large networks is that the vertex connectivities follow a scale-free power-law distribution. This feature was found to be a consequence of two generic mechanisms: (i) networks expand continuously by the addition of new vertices, and (ii) new vertices attach preferentially to sites that are already well connected. A model based on these two ingredients reproduces the observed stationary scale-free distributions, which indicates that the development of large networks is governed by robust self-organizing phenomena that go beyond the particulars of the individual systems.", author = "Barab{\'a}si, {Albert L{\'a}szl{\'o}} and R{\'e}ka Albert", year = "1999", month = oct, day = "15", doi = "10.1126/science.286.5439.509", language = "English (US)", volume = "286", pages = "509--512", journal = "Science", issn = "0036-8075", publisher = "American Association for the Advancement of Science", number = "5439" }
